key_sub: In-situ: protect in the wild; ex-situ: protect outside the natural home.
body_html:
How to think about it

Biodiversity exists at the genetic, species and ecological levels. It is highest in the tropics and falls towards the poles; species richness rises with area up to a limit (Humboldt's species–area relationship). India has about 2.4% of the world's land but about 8.1% of its species.

The main causes of biodiversity loss are habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and co-extinctions — the 'Evil Quartet'. Conservation is in-situ (biosphere reserves, national parks, sanctuaries, sacred groves, hotspots) or ex-situ (zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks, cryopreservation).

Example

Seed bank is?

outside the habitat

Answer: ex-situ conservation

Example

Cichlids lost in Lake Victoria due to?

alien species

Answer: the Nile perch

Common mistakes

  • Calling zoos in-situ conservation.
  • Saying biodiversity rises towards the poles.
  • Thinking hotspots have few endemic species.
